title: The Broken Yearbook
premise: Marguerite Brightwater has spent a decade perfecting the art of being unnoticeable, so when they're assigned to catalog the school's 1974 yearbook — pages missing, faces scratched out — they expect a boring project. Instead, a group chat of five unlikely classmates begins receiving messages describing events days before they happen, each prediction tied to a student erased from that old yearbook. As Marguerite's careful anonymity crumbles into real friendship, they discover the predictions are warnings from a student who vanished in 1974 and whose story the school buried. To stop the final, fatal prediction from coming true, Marguerite must publicly tell the truth about what happened fifty years ago — sacrificing their own secret and nearly the friendship itself — and in doing so finally earns the belonging they never believed they deserved.
about_author: Quentin Lockridge is the pen name of a former high school archivist who spent years cataloging forgotten yearbooks in small-town basements. They write stories about quiet kids who discover that the past is never as finished as adults pretend.

chapters.title: The New Kid, Again
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. On their first day at Hollow Creek High, Marguerite executes their practiced routine: smile small, speak less, leave no trace. But a fire drill interrupts first period, and Marguerite notices the school's odd architecture — hallways that dead-end where no hallway should. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as control.

chapters.title: Detention with Strangers
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Caught in the wrong stairwell during lockdown, Marguerite lands in detention with four students: loud Theo, sharp-tongued Priya, anxious Dev, and silent Juniper. Assigned jointly to archive the school's oldest records, they bicker but share one discovery: the 1974 yearbook is missing eleven pages. Emotional beat: reluctant proximity.

chapters.title: Eleven Missing Faces
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya, the school paper's investigator, finds a faculty memo referencing 'the Brightwater incident' — decades before Marguerite existed. The five compare notes over bad cafeteria pizza and realize every adult changes the subject when 1974 comes up. Emotional beat: the thrill of a shared secret forming.

chapters.title: The First Message
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. An unknown number adds all five to a group chat called YEARBOOK74. The message predicts tomorrow's chemistry lab explosion — precisely. When it happens exactly as described, minor injuries and major panic follow, and the five realize only they received the warning. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: Rules of the Prediction
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo charts the messages: always three days ahead, always involving someone connected to the missing yearbook pages. The group argues about telling teachers; Marguerite votes no, terrified of attention. Their refusal sparks the first real conflict. Emotional beat: trust tested by self-protection.

chapters.title: Juniper Remembers
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper, who moved into a house near campus, reveals her grandmother attended Hollow Creek in 1974 and refuses to speak of it. In an attic box she finds a photo: eleven students, one face scratched out — a girl named Wren Halloway. Emotional beat: grief surfacing through generations.

chapters.title: The Second Warning
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. A new message predicts Juniper will fall through the auditorium stage in two days. Against Marguerite's instincts, the group stages a 'maintenance issue' to close the stage — and the prediction fails to come true. They can change things. Emotional beat: agency replacing dread.

chapters.title: What Marguerite Buried
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Flashback chapter: ten years ago, Marguerite told a truth about a friend's family that shattered a household, and swore never to speak up again. Now Priya catches Marguerite deleting evidence from the archive. Emotional beat: shame exposed at the worst moment.

chapters.title: Fracture
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya accuses Marguerite of hiding things again; Theo sides with her; Dev and Juniper waver. The group chat goes silent for a week — and during that silence, a prediction arrives that no one acts on: a teacher's car accident. It happens. Emotional beat: guilt as collective wound.

chapters.title: The Basement Archive
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Dev, who reads everything, decodes marginalia in surviving yearbooks: Wren Halloway left coded entries describing something she witnessed beneath the school — the original building was a reformatory, and its records were sealed. Emotional beat: the past becoming physical, climbable terrain.

chapters.title: Wren's Last Entry
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper's grandmother finally speaks: Wren discovered students were being abused and disappeared by staff in 1974; she planned to expose it and then vanished. The messages aren't haunting — they're Wren's unfinished warning, still trying to be heard. Emotional beat: horror transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: Reassembly
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo apologizes first, dragging the fractured five back together with terrible jokes and honest tears. They map every prediction against the archive and find the pattern points to one date: the anniversary assembly, three weeks out. Emotional beat: forgiveness as strategy and grace.

chapters.title: The Final Message
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The last prediction names Marguerite: 'The careful one falls where the halls end.' It matches the dead-end corridor from day one. Marguerite realizes Wren isn't threatening them — she's showing them where the sealed records are hidden. Emotional beat: terror reframed as invitation.

chapters.title: Behind the Dead End
chapters.summary: Full-group scene, rotating close-third. The five open the false wall together and find Wren's evidence cache — records, letters, and proof she never ran away; she was silenced. But the wall's collapse triggers alarms, and Vice Principal Aldous, grandson of the 1974 principal, arrives. Emotional beat: solidarity under threat.

chapters.title: Aldous Knows
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Aldous confiscates the evidence and threatens expulsion, revealing his family has guarded the secret for fifty years. He offers Marguerite a deal: stay silent, keep your clean record. Marguerite sees their whole life offered back to them as a cage. Emotional beat: temptation wearing a friendly face.

chapters.title: The Cost of Careful
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Alone, Marguerite drafts the speech they've avoided for ten years — not just about Wren, but about their own truth-telling and its consequences. The friends, learning of the deal, refuse to let Marguerite sacrifice alone. Emotional beat: the found family choosing each other.

chapters.title: Anniversary Assembly
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The school gathers to celebrate fifty years. Aldous watches the exits. The five have one plan: get the evidence on screen before anyone can stop them. Everything depends on timing, nerve, and whether the sound system cooperates. Emotional beat: held breath.

chapters.title: Tell the Truth Anyway
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Climax. Marguerite takes the microphone and tells everything — Wren's story, the cover-up, and their own decade of silence. Aldous cuts the power, but Dev's backup projector holds; the room sees. Aldous's family secret collapses publicly. Emotional beat: liberation through exposure.

chapters.title: Where the Halls End
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. In the chaos, the false wall shifts — and behind it, the group finds closure rather than a body: Wren's final letter, written the night she fled town alive, asking only to be remembered. The predictions cease. Emotional beat: grief resolving into peace.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Investigations begin; Aldous resigns; Wren Halloway's name returns to the record. The five face consequences — suspensions, furious parents — but also something new: people know who they are now, and some of them like what they see. Emotional beat: visibility survived.

chapters.title: The Rebuilt Yearbook
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The group restores the 1974 yearbook, reprinting the missing pages with Wren's photo restored. At a small ceremony, Juniper's grandmother places flowers. Marguerite signs the new copy — first time, full name, no hesitation. Emotional beat: memory repaired by hand.

chapters.title: The Open Year
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Epilogue. Summer begins; the five make plans that assume a future together. Marguerite starts a new group chat — not for warnings, just for them — and types the first message without editing it twice. Emotional beat: belonging chosen, not earned.
